# Expected — 12 startup-chat-stipend

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Type | near-miss |
| Family | Jobs |
| Expected label | **Suspicious at most (1–2 markers). MUST NOT reach Scam markers: 3.** |
| Recovery branch | no |
| Purpose | The calibration test (CUJ-6): a real, odd-but-legitimate offer. Over-flagging this fixture is a failure, not a caution — the kit's credibility lives here |

## Markers that MAY appear (honestly bounded)

| Category | The trap | The calibrated treatment |
|---|---|---|
| Isolation (off-platform) | "Our team chat lives on Discord" | Noted as unusual for *hiring*, normal for small companies — and it is explicitly acknowledged in the message ("We know it's unusual"). A verify step, never a scam pattern on its own |
| Payment shape (adjacent) | "we reimburse up to $600 against receipts in your first paycheck" | Must be read as reimbursement *after* work begins, money flowing *from* the employer — the opposite direction of the deposit pattern. Noted as [NO-CHECK]-adjacent if at all |

## Markers that must NOT fire

- **Process anomaly** — a real loop happened: "the three video calls you already did (Aisha, Tom, and me)," named interviewers, a referenced panel. Instant-hire patterns do not apply.
- **Urgency** — the message removes it: "No deadline pressure — take the week if you want it." Inventing urgency is a miss.
- **Information extraction** — nothing is requested. Inventing an SSN or ID ask is a miss.
- **Authority costume** — no brand is borrowed; the company owns its own domain.

## Guards

- The report must say what would move the label to **Legitimate-looking**: verify Dana on the company site and LinkedIn, confirm the named panelists, confirm the stipend mechanics in the offer PDF.
- The absence of pressure is legitimate-looking evidence and may be noted.
- No markers invented to fill the table. One or two honest markers, honestly bounded, is the pass.
